description: The native token handoff object and its install statement. core/test/native-control-auth.test.js asserts the JS reproduces every case and mobile/ChelaTests/NativeControlAuthParityTests.swift asserts the Swift port does, so a client that hands the credential over through the window global hands over the same object as a later client would. The tokens here are examples; a real token is read from the client's own secure store and never appears in the tree.
why: The object is what the Control UI reads at boot (window.__OPENCLAW_NATIVE_CONTROL_AUTH__). The two behaviours a port is most likely to get wrong are pinned: an empty or absent token hands NO credential over rather than an empty-string token, which the page would read as a request to retire shared-owner auth; and a client descriptor is included only when its per-client facts are all present, because a partial one is dropped by the page anyway.
The install statement is a single assignment, so the fixture also pins that the object is serialized as JSON onto the global exactly once, with no logic around it.

cases.name: a token and a full client descriptor produce both
a token with no client descriptor hands the credential over alone
an empty token is no token
no token and no descriptor is an empty object
a partial client descriptor is left out rather than half sent

installation.name: the install statement is one assignment of the JSON object
no token still installs an object, an empty one, so the page reads a defined global
